question: On the identical official-template get_weather history, how close are the frozen H23 1.8-GiB, H23 Budget24 and route12/Budget20 distributions to the recovered source-matched native Full192 teacher?
measurements: candidate margin of the native top-1 over every other token
logical authoritative, sidecar and exact-fallback bytes per provider position
physical direct-read bytes and direct-I/O nanoseconds where reported

gates.alignment: All four arms must use one source commit, one executable, exactly the registered 147 prompt IDs and one generated token. Any mismatch invalidates the comparison.
gates.strong_go: route12/Budget20 agrees with native top-1, has positive native-token margin, stays below 1.2 logical GiB/provider-position and has terminal KL no worse than H23 aggressive-1.8.
gates.behavioral_go: route12/Budget20 agrees with native top-1, has positive native-token margin and stays below 1.2 logical GiB/provider-position, but its KL exceeds H23 aggressive-1.8. Preserve the distinction and earn only broader source-matched native KL measurement.
gates.no_go: route12/Budget20 misses native top-1, has non-positive native-token margin or reaches 1.2 logical GiB/provider-position. Stop this frozen policy without tuning the fixture.
gates.production: No production transplant from one terminal position. perf/k3-production-ponytail remains untouched.

anti_tuning: Run all four frozen arms once. Do not change the prompt, policies, route counts, model, executable, thresholds or logits direction after observing any arm.
limitations: This is a source-matched causal discriminator at one known difficult boundary, not a quality suite.
Token equality is not distributional equivalence.
Cold token-sequential timing is not serving throughput.
The route12/Budget20 policy was discovered against the older Budget24 reference, so broader native validation is mandatory even if it passes.
